title: The finite-tuple presentation of a cartesian monoidal infinity category
statement:
Use the infinity-category, mapping-space and universe conventions of [def-coef-complete-algebroid], enlarging universes when necessary. Use the cocartesian fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Let $\mathcal C$ be an infinity category with finite products, meaning that $\operatorname{Map}(t,\prod_i c_i)\simeq\prod_i\operatorname{Map}(t,c_i)$ for every finite family, including the terminal object for the empty family. Let $\mathsf{Fin}_*$ be finite pointed sets, $\langle n\rangle=\{*,1,\ldots,n\}$. There is a canonical cartesian symmetric monoidal infinity category $r_{\mathcal C}:\mathcal C^{\times}\to N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$: a cocartesian fibration with fiber $\mathcal C^n$ over $\langle n\rangle$, whose inert projections select the coordinates. Here inert means each non-basepoint of the target has exactly one preimage. For tuples $c=(c_1,\ldots,c_n)$ and $d=(d_1,\ldots,d_m)$, the mapping space over a pointed map $\alpha:\langle n\rangle\to\langle m\rangle$ is naturally
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C^{\times}}^{\alpha}(c,d)\simeq\prod_{j=1}^{m}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}\left(\prod_{\alpha(i)=j}c_i,d_j\right).$$
Composition substitutes the block maps, using the canonical regrouping of products; coordinates mapped to $*$ are discarded. A lift over $\alpha$ is $r_{\mathcal C}$-cocartesian precisely when all displayed component maps are equivalences. A finite-product-preserving functor $h:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ induces a strong symmetric monoidal functor $h^{\times}:\mathcal C^{\times}\to\mathcal D^{\times}$, where strong means preserving all cocartesian arrows over $N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$, acting coordinatewise and on block maps by $h$ and its product comparisons. The construction is functorial with all higher coherences; its choices, with their specified product cones, form a contractible space.

source.place: Construction 2.4.1.4, Proposition 2.4.1.5 and Corollaries 2.4.1.8-2.4.1.9; tuple mapping spaces are the component form of the product-diagram construction. Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical result.

proof.text: Define an ordinary category $\Gamma^{\times}$: its objects are $(\langle n\rangle,S)$ with $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and an arrow over $\alpha:\langle n\rangle\to\langle m\rangle$ exists precisely when $\alpha^{-1}(T)\subseteq S$; it is then unique over $\alpha$. Composition is composition of pointed maps, since inverse images preserve inclusions. The projection $v:N(\Gamma^{\times})\to N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$ is a cartesian fibration in [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Indeed every inner $2$-horn fills by composition, and every higher inner horn fills by its prescribed string of arrows. For a target $(\langle m\rangle,T)$ the lift of $\alpha$ with source $(\langle n\rangle,\alpha^{-1}T)$ is cartesian: the missing edge of a right outer $2$-horn over $\beta$ exists exactly when $(\alpha\beta)^{-1}T\subseteq R$, equivalently $\beta^{-1}(\alpha^{-1}T)\subseteq R$, and is unique. In higher right outer horns all edges are already specified; each missing triangle commutes because its base triangle commutes and there is at most one arrow over a specified base arrow. Thus the horn criterion holds. Its fiber is $N(B_n)$, where $B_n$ is the finite subset poset with reverse inclusion.

source.place: Notation 2.4.1.2; explicit nerve/horn verification of its cartesian projection

proof.text: Apply [lem-cbc-enhanced-relative-exponential] with base $N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$, cartesian fibration $v$ from step 1, and target $\mathcal C$. It constructs an actual simplicial set $Q$ whose simplices over $\sigma:\Delta^k\to N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$ are maps $\Delta^k\times_{N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)}N(\Gamma^{\times})\to\mathcal C$. The lemma says that $Q$ is a quasicategory and $q:Q\to N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$ a cocartesian fibration, with fiber $\operatorname{Fun}(N(B_n),\mathcal C)$. Its cocartesian-edge criterion says that the arrows over $\alpha$ whose maps $f(\alpha^{-1}T)\to g(T)$ are equivalences for every subset $T$ are cocartesian. In particular transport is $\alpha_!f(T)=f(\alpha^{-1}T)$: over the arrow $\alpha$, the indexing category retracts onto $B_n$ by sending $(0,S)$ to $S$ and $(1,T)$ to $\alpha^{-1}T$. A crossing arrow exists exactly when $\alpha^{-1}T\subseteq S$, so this is a functor; composing with $f$ gives a lift taking cartesian edges to identities. This description also retains the higher simplices supplied by the lemma.

source.place: Construction 2.4.1.4 and Proposition 2.4.1.5(1),(2); HTT Corollary 3.2.2.13 via the existing relative-exponential node

proof.text: Let $A_n\subseteq B_n$ be the full, discrete subposet of singleton subsets, with inclusion $j_n$. For $S\in B_n$, the objects of $(A_n)_{\geq S}$ are exactly $\{i\}$ for $i\in S$. Thus [lem-coef-infinity-finite-poset-kan-extension], in its right-hand form, gives a coherent right extension $R_n(c)$ of every tuple $c=(c_i)$, with $R_n(c)(S)\simeq\prod_{i\in S}c_i$ and the specified product projections. Only finite discrete limits are required here, so the hypothesis is exactly finite products, including $R_n(c)(\varnothing)$ terminal. Let $P_n$ be the full subcategory of $\operatorname{Fun}(N(B_n),\mathcal C)$ of these product diagrams. The same lemma's unit and counit identify $f$ with $R_nj_n^*f$ whenever $f\in P_n$: at every $S$ the unit is the comparison of the same product cone, and hence an equivalence by the mapping-space universal property. The componentwise-equivalence criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] makes this a functor-category equivalence; its closure assertion ensures that these functor categories and their full subcategories are quasicategories. Its adjunction formula, restricted to $P_n$, gives $\operatorname{Map}(f,g)\simeq\operatorname{Map}(j_n^*f,j_n^*g)$ because $g\simeq R_nj_n^*g$. Consequently restriction gives $P_n\simeq\mathcal C^n$. For $n=0$ the input poset is empty and its right extension is a terminal object; $P_0\simeq *$.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 2.4.1.5(4), singleton-subset restriction and right Kan extension

proof.text:
Define $\mathcal C^{\times}$ to be the full simplicial subset of $Q$ on vertices in the $P_n$. It is stable under the cocartesian transports of step 2. To check this without choosing coherent products, let $f\in P_n$ and put $g(T)=f(\alpha^{-1}T)$. For every $x\in\mathcal C$, the product-cone equivalences give
$$\operatorname{Map}(x,g(T))\simeq\prod_{i\in\alpha^{-1}T}\operatorname{Map}(x,f(\{i\}))\simeq\prod_{j\in T}\operatorname{Map}(x,f(\alpha^{-1}\{j\})).$$
The middle equality is merely the regrouping of a finite disjoint union, since distinct non-basepoints have disjoint inverse images. The maps are exactly the cone maps $g(T)\to g(\{j\})$, so $g\in P_m$. The full-subcategory assertion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] supplies quasicategory closure. Fullness supplies the inner-horn fillers and retains the ambient cocartesian lifts; those lifts satisfy the mapping-space cocartesian squares also when tested on the full subcategory: [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] turns the horn-cocartesian lifts of the inner fibration $q$ into homotopy-pullback squares for every test vertex, the mapping spaces of a full subcategory are the ambient ones, and the same criterion converts the squares back into the horn condition for the restricted inner fibration, as in [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening]. Hence $r_{\mathcal C}:\mathcal C^{\times}\to N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$ is a cocartesian fibration with the fibers of step 3. For an inert map, every retained block is a singleton, so its transport selects the indicated coordinates. These are precisely the required Segal equivalences, which make this fibration a symmetric monoidal infinity category in [lem-coef-symmetric-monoidal-segal-classification]. Its fold operation is finite product and its nullary operation is terminal, so the structure is cartesian.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.1.5(3),(4),(5); disjoint-block verification of transport stability

proof.text:
Fix $f\in P_n$, $g\in P_m$ and $\alpha$. The explicit cocartesian lift of step 2 ends at $a(T)=f(\alpha^{-1}T)\in P_m$. Its cocartesian square, which this horn-cocartesian edge of the inner fibration $r_{\mathcal C}$ satisfies by [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] (the intrinsic square of [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening]), pulled back to $\operatorname{id}_{\langle m\rangle}$ in the mapping space of the base, identifies the mapping space over $\alpha$ with $\operatorname{Map}_{P_m}(a,g)$. This uses the same node's identification of the simplicial fiber with the infinity-categorical fiber. Applying the right Kan adjunction of [lem-coef-infinity-finite-poset-kan-extension] to $g\simeq R_mj_m^*g$ identifies this with
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C^m}((f(\alpha^{-1}\{j\}))_j,(g(\{j\}))_j)=\prod_{j=1}^m\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(f(\alpha^{-1}\{j\}),g(\{j\})).$$
The equality follows degreewise from the product simplicial-set definition of functor categories and mapping spaces. Substitute the product-cone identifications of step 3 and write $c_i=f(\{i\})$, $d_j=g(\{j\})$. This gives exactly the asserted tuple mapping-space formula, naturally, rather than merely a bijection on homotopy classes.

source.place: Component mapping-space consequence of Construction 2.4.1.4 and Proposition 2.4.1.5

proof.text:
For a second pointed map $\beta:\langle m\rangle\to\langle l\rangle$, the indexing diagram has the equality $(\beta\alpha)^{-1}U=\alpha^{-1}(\beta^{-1}U)$. If arrows have singleton components $u_j:\prod_{\alpha(i)=j}c_i\to d_j$ and $v_k:\prod_{\beta(j)=k}d_j\to e_k$, their composite component is
$$\prod_{\beta(\alpha(i))=k}c_i\simeq\prod_{\beta(j)=k}\prod_{\alpha(i)=j}c_i\xrightarrow{\prod_j u_j}\prod_{\beta(j)=k}d_j\xrightarrow{v_k}e_k.$$
The right Kan adjunction from step 5 identifies this formula with restriction of the composite of the original diagram maps; their projections are the displayed $u_j$ and $v_k$. Coordinates mapped to $*$ belong to no inverse image of a non-basepoint and are therefore discarded. Identities restrict to identity block maps. This is a calculation in the already constructed simplicial category $Q$, so associativity and every face/degeneracy compatibility come from its simplices; no inference from binary coherence to higher coherence is made.

source.place: Construction 2.4.1.4, composition on diagrams; explicit substitution formula

proof.text: An arrow over $\alpha$ factors, by the mapping-space equivalence in step 5, as the chosen cocartesian lift followed by a fiber arrow $w:a\to g$. The mapping-space squares of [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion], which characterize horn-cocartesian edges of the inner fibration $r_{\mathcal C}$ in both directions (the intrinsic squares of [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening]), show that this arrow is cocartesian if and only if $w$ is an equivalence: in the forward direction, testing on every $z\in P_m$ yields equivalences $\operatorname{Map}(g,z)\to\operatorname{Map}(a,z)$. At $z=a$, the inverse image of $\operatorname{id}_a$ is a map $\ell:g\to a$ with $\ell w=\operatorname{id}_a$. At $z=g$, the map obtained by applying the inverse to $w$ is $\operatorname{id}_g$; since $(w\ell)w=w=\operatorname{id}_g w$ and precomposition with $w$ is an equivalence, this gives $w\ell=\operatorname{id}_g$. In the reverse direction, precomposition by an equivalence preserves each of the cocartesian mapping-space squares. The fully faithful restriction $P_m\simeq\mathcal C^m$ from step 3 detects equivalences, and in a product category an inverse is specified coordinatewise, so $w$ is an equivalence exactly when each displayed block component is. This also shows that no additional cocartesian arrows arise on restricting from $Q$. When $m=0$ the criterion is vacuous and the fiber is terminal; when a block is empty its source is terminal but its component must still be an equivalence.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.1.5(2),(3); necessity as well as sufficiency on the full product-diagram subcategory

proof.text: For $h:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ preserving finite products, postcompose every simplex of $Q_{\mathcal C}$ with $h$. This defines a simplicial map over $N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$ and preserves the full subcategories of product diagrams, since $h$ carries every specified finite product cone to a product cone. It gives $h^{\times}$. A cocartesian edge sends the cartesian indexing edges to equivalences by [lem-cbc-enhanced-relative-exponential]; postcomposition preserves equivalence edges (apply $h$ to their two inverse triangles), so $h^{\times}$ preserves cocartesian arrows. Equivalently use the component criterion of step 7. It is therefore strong in the convention of [lem-coef-symmetric-monoidal-segal-classification]. On singleton evaluation it is coordinatewise $h$, and on a block its source comparison is the inverse of the canonical product-preservation equivalence $h(\prod c_i)\simeq\prod h(c_i)$, followed by the image of the block map. Postcomposition commutes strictly with composition, identities and simplicial operators in this model; parameterized maps give the corresponding higher coherences.

source.place: Construction 2.4.1.4, functoriality by postcomposition; compare Corollaries 2.4.1.8-2.4.1.9

proof.text: There is no product choice in the definition of the total simplicial set: all product diagrams with their cones are retained. The only choices in its tuple presentation are the right Kan extensions and the specified restriction identifications from step 3. The adjunction in [lem-coef-infinity-finite-poset-kan-extension] makes these universal arrows for $j_n^*$. Apply [lem-coef-parametric-universal-arrows] to that restriction functor, with domain all tuples: it says explicitly that the universal-arrow choices, including the coherent extension functor and its counit, form a contractible space, and that the mapping equivalences remain natural for arbitrary simplicial parameters. This justifies both the contractible choices of tuple/product-cone identifications and their higher coherence. Together with the fixed relative-exponential construction and functorial postcomposition in step 8, it proves the asserted canonicity and coherent functoriality of the construction.

source.place: Right Kan product-cone choices in Proposition 2.4.1.5; construction-level uniqueness compatible with Corollaries 2.4.1.8-2.4.1.9

lean.statement: theorem cartesian_operadic_envelope (C : SSet.{u}) [Quasicategory C] (hC : HasFiniteProducts C) : Assertions C
lean.note: The specified envelope is the real full product-diagram subcomplex of the published relative exponential. Subset cones are the canonical pointwise right Kan cones. The block comparison is normalized on all parameter simplices, and cocartesianness is tested on those actual components. Coherent functoriality uses actual parameter postcomposition; choices are the actual category of lifts of singleton restriction. Helpers belong to this statement; no definition chooses data from a postponed existence theorem.
